Article 22

Parents have the responsibility to prevent acts of violence against women and children, including:
a. fostering love, affection and mutual respect in the family;
b. providing assistance to victims; and
c. reporting every form of domestic violence.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 30

1. The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. In addition to the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence, PPT takes preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children.
3. PPT reports the implementation of the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence as well as preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children to the Mayor through the Agency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE CITY OF BITUNG

NUMBER 8 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN THE CITY OF BITUNG

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF BITUNG,

Considering:

a. that the guarantee of respect, protection and fulfillment of Human Rights for every Indonesian Citizen in the Region is a duty that must be carried out by the Regional Government; b. that the City of Bitung as a rapidly developing industrial city as one of the economic centers in the Province of North Sulawesi, has created many job opportunities so that many people from various areas outside the City of Bitung come to work within the territory of the City of Bitung and have the potential to create social friction which can result in the vulnerability of women and children to become victims of acts of violence; c. that in the framework of implementing regional autonomy which refers to Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b and Article 236 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, particularly in the field of women's empowerment and child protection which is included in concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Regional Government, namely mandatory government affairs not related to basic services, the Region establishes a Regional Regulation; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence in the City of Bitung; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143); 3. Law Number 7 of 1990 concerning the Establishment of the Municipality of Second Level Region of Bitung (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1990 Number 52, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3421); 4. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 5. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4235), as has been amended several times most recently by Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 99, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5882); 6. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 7. Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4720); 8. Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formulation of Legislation (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2011 Number 82, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5234); 9. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679); 10. Government Regulation Number 4 of 2006 concerning the Implementation and Cooperation for the Recovery of Victims of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 15, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 64); 11. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 2 of 2008 concerning the Implementation of Women's Protection; 12. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 3 of 2008 concerning the Implementation of Child Protection; 13. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards (SPM) for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence (State News of the Republic of Indonesia of 2010 Number 56); 14. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 5 of 2010 concerning Guidelines for the Establishment and Development of Integrated Service Centers; 15. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 2 of 2011 concerning the Empowerment of Child Victims of Violence; 16. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 19 of 2011 concerning the Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence; 17. Regulation of the Minister of Home Affairs Number 80 of 2015 concerning the Formulation of Regional Legal Products (State News of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 2036); as has been amended by Regulation of the Minister of Home Affairs Number 120 of 2018 concerning the Amendment to Regulation of the Minister of Home Affairs Number 80 of 2015 concerning the Formulation of Regional Legal Products (State News of the Republic of Indonesia of 2018 Number 157);

Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

Family as referred to in Article 11 letter c has full responsibility to protect women and children from all forms of acts of violence.

Article 34

Psychosocial services are services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of women and children who are victims of violence, including the provision of safe houses to protect women and children who are victims of violence from various threats and intimidation against women and children who are victims of violence and to provide social support so that women and children who are victims of violence have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving their problems.

Article 33

1. PPT may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
2. PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses.
3. In the event that PPT does not yet have a Safe House, women and children who are victims of acts of violence are referred to PPT that has a Safe House.

Article 19

1. Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to protection of women's and children's rights to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.
2. PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 42

1. The Regional Government shall conduct guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 43

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (1) shall be conducted in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards stipulated by laws and regulations.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF BITUNG,

Considering:

a. that the guarantee of respect, protection and fulfillment of Human Rights for every Indonesian Citizen in the Region is a duty that must be carried out by the Regional Government; b. that the City of Bitung as a rapidly developing industrial city as one of the economic centers in the Province of North Sulawesi, has created many job opportunities so that many people from various areas outside the City of Bitung come to work within the territory of the City of Bitung and have the potential to create social friction which can result in the vulnerability of women and children to become victims of acts of violence; c. that in the framework of implementing regional autonomy which refers to Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b and Article 236 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, particularly in the field of women's empowerment and child protection which is included in concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Regional Government, namely mandatory government affairs not related to basic services, the Region establishes a Regional Regulation; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence in the City of Bitung; In View of:

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

Considering:

a. that the guarantee of respect, protection and fulfillment of Human Rights for every Indonesian Citizen in the Region is a duty that must be carried out by the Regional Government; b. that the City of Bitung as a rapidly developing industrial city as one of the economic centers in the Province of North Sulawesi, has created many job opportunities so that many people from various areas outside the City of Bitung come to work within the territory of the City of Bitung and have the potential to create social friction which can result in the vulnerability of women and children to become victims of acts of violence; c. that in the framework of implementing regional autonomy which refers to Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b and Article 236 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, particularly in the field of women's empowerment and child protection which is included in concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Regional Government, namely mandatory government affairs not related to basic services, the Region establishes a Regional Regulation; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence in the City of Bitung; In View of:

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER VIII

EMPOWERMENT AND REHABILITATION

Article 40

1. Empowerment of women who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (1) letter d shall be implemented by means of:
a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
3. Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence may be implemented at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government or organized by private parties.
4. Establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented by coordinating with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 19

1. Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to protection of women's and children's rights to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.
2. PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Mayor Regulation.

Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 43

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (1) shall be conducted in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards stipulated by laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

REUNIFICATION

Article 39

In order to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:
a. provide transportation costs and other needs for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to return home to their families;
b. provide and finance accompanying personnel to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families; and
c. coordinate with the Government, Regional Government of the place of residence of women and children who are victims of acts of violence and the Indonesian National Police to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence

3.6.text:
Article 33

1. PPT may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
2. PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses.
3. In the event that PPT does not yet have a Safe House, women and children who are victims of acts of violence are referred to PPT that has a Safe House.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 32

1. PPT has a counseling division in assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. The counseling division as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. legal division;
b. health division;
c. spiritual division; and
d. psychology division.

Article 34

Psychosocial services are services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of women and children who are victims of violence, including the provision of safe houses to protect women and children who are victims of violence from various threats and intimidation against women and children who are victims of violence and to provide social support so that women and children who are victims of violence have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving their problems.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.

a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.

CHAPTER V

PROVISION OF SERVICES, ASSISTANCE AND RECOVERY FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN WHO ARE VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Psychosocial services are services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of women and children who are victims of violence, including the provision of safe houses to protect women and children who are victims of violence from various threats and intimidation against women and children who are victims of violence and to provide social support so that women and children who are victims of violence have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving their problems.

Article 29

The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out by the Regional Government by establishing PPT.

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

REUNIFICATION

Article 39

In order to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER VIII

EMPOWERMENT AND REHABILITATION

Article 40

1. Empowerment of women who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (1) letter d shall be implemented by means of:
a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
3. Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence may be implemented at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government or organized by private parties.
4. Establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented by coordinating with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

Article 30

1. The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. In addition to the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence, PPT takes preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children.
3. PPT reports the implementation of the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence as well as preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children to the Mayor through the Agency.

Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

Article 33

1. PPT may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
2. PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses.
3. In the event that PPT does not yet have a Safe House, women and children who are victims of acts of violence are referred to PPT that has a Safe House.

b. acts without the consent of women and children who become victims of exploitation, including but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits, whether physical/material in nature or non-physical/non-material; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of women and children who become victims of exploitation to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and

Psychosocial services are services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of women and children who are victims of violence, including the provision of safe houses to protect women and children who are victims of violence from various threats and intimidation against women and children who are victims of violence and to provide social support so that women and children who are victims of violence have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving their problems.

c. services; and
d. performance.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE CITY OF BITUNG

NUMBER 8 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN THE CITY OF BITUNG

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF BITUNG,

Considering:

a. that the guarantee of respect, protection and fulfillment of Human Rights for every Indonesian Citizen in the Region is a duty that must be carried out by the Regional Government; b. that the City of Bitung as a rapidly developing industrial city as one of the economic centers in the Province of North Sulawesi, has created many job opportunities so that many people from various areas outside the City of Bitung come to work within the territory of the City of Bitung and have the potential to create social friction which can result in the vulnerability of women and children to become victims of acts of violence; c. that in the framework of implementing regional autonomy which refers to Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b and Article 236 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, particularly in the field of women's empowerment and child protection which is included in concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Regional Government, namely mandatory government affairs not related to basic services, the Region establishes a Regional Regulation; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence in the City of Bitung; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143); 3. Law Number 7 of 1990 concerning the Establishment of the Municipality of Second Level Region of Bitung (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1990 Number 52, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3421); 4. I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 38

1. PPT shall report the implementation of protection provision for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to the Mayor through the Agency.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
4. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at the latest once every 3 (three) months.

Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 19

1. Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to protection of women's and children's rights to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.
2. PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Mayor Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
3. Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence may be implemented at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government or organized by private parties.
4. Establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented by coordinating with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

REUNIFICATION

Article 39

In order to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:
a. provide transportation costs and other needs for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to return home to their families;
b. provide and finance accompanying personnel to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families; and
c. coordinate with the Government, Regional Government of the place of residence of women and children who are victims of acts of violence and the Indonesian National Police to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER V

PROVISION OF SERVICES, ASSISTANCE AND RECOVERY FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN WHO ARE VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 38

1. PPT shall report the implementation of protection provision for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to the Mayor through the Agency.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
4. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at the latest once every 3 (three) months.

Article 30

1. The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. In addition to the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence, PPT takes preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children.
3. PPT reports the implementation of the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence as well as preventive measures against acts of violence against women and children to the Mayor through the Agency.

I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those threatening women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, seeing this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. This Regional Regulation regulates the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein so as to suppress the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition it also regulates the institutions that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection implemented by the Regional Government.

CHAPTER VIII

EMPOWERMENT AND REHABILITATION

Article 40

1. Empowerment of women who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (1) letter d shall be implemented by means of:
a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
3. Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence may be implemented at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government or organized by private parties.
4. Establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented by coordinating with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

CHAPTER III

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

General

Article 28

1. Services for assistance and recovery of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. empowerment of women;
b. rehabilitation of children;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 19

1. Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to protection of women's and children's rights to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.
2. PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Mayor Regulation.
